card.title: Biot-Savart to Ampere — field of currents

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Moving charges feel F = qv×B (Lorentz) — perpendicular to both motion and field, so magnetism bends paths without doing work. Every current element contributes dB = (μ₀/4π)·Idl×r̂/r² (Biot-Savart); symmetric layouts surrender instead to Ampere's ∮B·dl = μ₀I. Parallel currents attract (antiparallel repel) with F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/2πd — the force that once DEFINED the ampere. Galvanometers read current by coil torque; shunts make ammeters, multipliers make voltmeters.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Lorentz: F = q(E + v×B)  ·  cyclotron: r = mv/qB, f = qB/2πm  ·  Biot-Savart → loop centre B = μ₀I/2R · solenoid B = μ₀nI · straight wire B = μ₀I/2πr  ·  Ampere: ∮B·dl = μ₀I_enclosed  ·  parallel wires: F/l = μ₀I₁I₂/2πd  ·  galvanometer: θ ∝ I; ammeter = G‖shunt, voltmeter = G+multiplier in series

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Biot-Savart needs steady currents; Ampere's loop must exploit symmetry (circle/coaxial path) to be useful. Lorentz magnetic part does no work (F ⊥ v) — speeds never change, only directions. Galvanometer linearity needs radial field + spring control; conversion formulas assume ideal shunt/multiplier.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Velocity selector: E = vB passes undeflected charges (mass spectrometry front end). Cyclotron frequency is mass-locked — the resonance trick behind accelerators and MRI magnets. Earth's field bends solar wind into aurorae. Tangent galvanometer is the classroom Biot-Savart application.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Field at a loop centre: each element Idl sits at distance R, all contributions point one way (right-hand grip) → B = Σ(μ₀/4π)Idl/R² = (μ₀I/4πR²)·2πR = μ₀I/2R. Ampere shortcut for a solenoid: rectangular loop gives B·L = μ₀nLI → B = μ₀nI, uniform inside, ~zero outside.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Biot-Savart integrates painfully without symmetry — Ampere rescues only symmetric cases. Classical orbits radiate and collapse (Bohr fixed the atom, not magnetism). Ferromagnets add domain physics no current-loop model predicts. Hall probes measure B; compasses only point.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Straight wire via Biot-Savart: integrate dB = (μ₀I/4π)(dl·sinθ/r²) along infinite length → B = μ₀I/2πr. Ampere check: circular loop around the wire, ∮B·dl = B·2πr = μ₀I — same result, one line. Parallel-wire force: wire 2 sits in B₁ = μ₀I₁/2πd, feels F = I₂LB₁ → F/l formula; direction by Fleming's left hand.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Symmetry word → Ampere loop matching it (circle for wires, rectangle for solenoids/sheets). Direction: right-hand grip for fields, Fleming's left for forces, Fleming's right for induced current. Galvanometer→ammeter: shunt in PARALLEL (low range extension); →voltmeter: multiplier in SERIES.
